packs.title: Between the Bricks
packs.promise: Find a new story in the details between Boston’s landmarks.

q.s: Read a church facade without needing to step inside.
st: Find a comfortable public-square view of Trinity Church’s exterior, keeping entrances free for the congregation.
Locate three contrasts: a smooth surface beside a rough one, a light area beside a dark one, and a curve beside a straight edge.
Record the contrasts in three brief observations. A detail from lower on the facade counts just as much as something high above.
Choose the contrast that most changes the building’s mood and give that mood one word.

q.s: Turn the library’s outside into the cover of an unwritten Boston story.
st: Choose a clear public-sidewalk view of the library’s Dartmouth Street facade across from Copley Square. Entering the library is optional and not part of this mission.
Collect three cover ingredients from the building: one shape, one texture, and one patch of light or shadow.
Imagine a book about your Boston day. Describe a cover using those three ingredients and give it a title of exactly six words.
Save your cover description and title as a field note, or use a facade photo as your cover with the title in its note.

q.s: Borrow the Garden’s pace for one small circuit.
st: Find the lagoon from an open Charles Street entrance. Choose a short stretch of the waterside path or an open route toward the footbridge.
Walk or roll only as far as feels comfortable, noticing the same tree, bridge, or roofline from two positions. Crossing the bridge is optional.
Compare what the new angle reveals and what it hides. Moving shadows or reflections count even when the lagoon has no boats.
At a clear resting point, record the two views and one reason this was worth taking slowly.

packs.title: Doors, Squares, Water
packs.promise: Notice the small details along a historic city route.

q.s: Find the details that make room for a city.
st: Choose an open public path position clear of the subway entrance.
Find a paving edge, a tree shape and a place designed for someone to pause.
Describe all three; an empty seating area or clear path edge can count.

q.s: Test what stays with you after a short look.
st: Choose a clear sidewalk view outside the chapel, without entering or climbing steps.
Look at the facade for fifteen seconds, then turn your attention away and recall three features.
Look back and check one memory against the building. Record what you kept or corrected.

q.s: Put three surfaces in an order of your own.
st: Choose a comfortable view from an open part or edge of the square.
Find three ground or boundary surfaces. Mentally order them from smoothest-looking to coarsest-looking using visible clues.
Record the order and one clue for your choice. Observe without touching sculpture or stepping into a gathering.

packs.title: History, Harbor and Home Teams
packs.promise: Explore Boston through revolutionary sites, the harbor, art and baseball.

q.s: Discover variety through the market’s own menus.
st: Read three current menus without blocking queues.
Choose an ingredient, a preparation and a dish name that interest you.
Record one question about the combination.

q.s: Look for how aquatic animals use different features.
st: Choose open exhibits included in your ticket.
Find a shelter, a water movement and a change in depth or space.
Read an official panel to explain one feature.

q.s: Respond to a historical presentation with an original question.
st: Join your booked visit and follow staff instructions.
Identify one stated historical fact and one question about whose perspective it represents.
After the visit, write an original two-sentence museum label separating fact from your question.
